To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) estradiol and progesterone have opposite effects on the growth of breast cells; (2) the effects of estradiol on growth are mediated by the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα); (3) the effects of progesterone are mediated by progesterone receptors (PRs); (4) the growth-promoting actions of estradiol are counteracted by progesterone; (5) the growth-inhibiting actions of progesterone depend on the presence

estradiol, the most potent endogenous human estrogen, stimulates cell growth and differentiation in human breast cells and that the effects of estradiol are mediated through its binding to the estrogen receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of sex steroids, particularly estradiol and progesterone, on human breast cells in vitro.
the effects of estrogens and progestins on the human breast.
the effects of sex steroids and other hormones on the development and growth of human breast cancer cells in vitro, and with their regulation of sex hormone receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of estradiol on breast cancer are complex and not fully understood.
the administration of progestogens in HRT regimens is not associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.
the use of oral contraceptives does not increase the risk of breast cancer in women who have never used them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the effects of estrogen and progestins on breast cancer risk are complex and not fully understood, and that the effects of progestins may be different from those of progesterone.
we have identified a new pathway for estradiol to activate the transcriptional activity of the progesterone receptor.

the results from our studies show that estrogen and progesterone receptors (ERs and PRs) are expressed in the majority of human breast cancers and that their expression levels can be used as prognostic markers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of estradiol in the form of estradiol valerate is a safe and effective treatment for the symptoms of menopause.
the effects of estradiol are mediated through the ERalpha receptor, while the effects of progesterone are mediated through the PR receptor.

we have shown for the first time that the effects of estradiol, progesterone, and progestins on human breast cells are mediated through the regulation of sex steroid receptor (SR) expression, not through direct effects on cell growth or differentiation.
